newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains on dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains on dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed slightly higher against the dollar but mildly lower against the basket of key foreign currencies on Wednesday in quiet trading, dealers said.
"At the opening of the trading day the shekel declined against the basket but rose against the dollar after the dollar dropped overnight on overseas markets," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
The U.S. currency fell after the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee decided not to raise interest rates.
"During the day trading was very quiet and volume was low. The fact that the dollar was very volatile abroad had no impact on local trading," the dealer said.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3880 shekels against 3.3910 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.7042 shekels against 3.7007 on Tuesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9765 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9896 on Tuesday, and against the mark at 2.0080 shekels compared with 1.9968 on Tuesday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3880 shekels.
